Subject: RFI: Vulnerability management and SBOM request

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our procurement for the CF infrastructure modernization program, our security team requested a short RFI focused on vulnerability management practices and SBOM availability. Could you please provide the following items by EOD Friday 9/18: 

- Short summary of SAST/DAST cadence and tooling used
- Patch/upgrade SLAs by severity and whether they differ for Dedicated customers
- Pen test (external) summary for last two quarters (high/critical findings + remediation status)
- SBOM snapshot for the core inference runtime and third-party libraries
- How you triage and notify customers for public CVEs affecting running instances

If you can attach a single package (PDF + SBOM + matrix) that would be perfect. We may have a follow-up narrow question after review.

Appreciate it,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Senior Security Manager, Catalyst Finance

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Vulnerability management and SBOM request

Hi team,

Draft package attached — I pulled the most relevant snippets below and included three attachments: VM_RFI_response_v1.pdf (customer-ready narrative), PenTest-Summary-Q2-2026.pdf (redacted findings), and SBOM-snapshot-2026-09-11.json. High-level answers: 

- SAST/DAST cadence & tooling:
  - SAST: weekly scheduled scans (Coverity + internal rule set) for all service repos; gating for PR merges to main.
  - DAST: quarterly external DAST engagement + continuous internal dynamic scans for the control plane endpoints (Burp/OWASP ZAP pipeline).
  - We maintain a central vuln tracker (internal Jira SUP-2345) with automated alerts into PagerDuty for infra-impacting findings.

- Patch / upgrade SLAs (standard hosted customers):
  - Severity/CVSS 9-10 (Critical): mitigation or hotfix published within 48 hours; optional emergency patch deployment within 72 hours if customer opts-in to auto-patch.
  - Severity 7-8.9 (High): remediation plan within 7 calendar days, patch rollout within 14 days.
  - Severity 4-6.9 (Medium): remediation in the next scheduled release (30 days typical).
  - Severity 0-3.9 (Low): tracked for routine dependency updates (quarterly).

- Dedicated customers / Private deployments:
  - We offer contracted SLA addendums for Dedicated customers that can include accelerated patching windows and optional managed patch service. See attached Patch-SLA-Matrix.csv (col A lists standard timelines; col B lists Dedicated add-on options).

- Pen tests:
  - Q2 2026 external pentest (EngageSec): 2 high findings (both related to misconfigured redirect logic in an internal admin console, CVE coverage not required for customers), 5 medium; all high findings closed within 18 days of discovery. Summary table in PenTest-Summary-Q2-2026.pdf.

- SBOM & third-party scanning:
  - We publish SBOM snapshots on request per major runtime release; attached is the runtime snapshot for 2026-09-11. We continuously scan dependencies with Snyk and internal heuristics; any public CVE with exploit maturity triggers an immediate review and patch acceleration.

- Customer notification & triage:
  - For public CVEs affecting running instances we: 1) create a triage ticket and severity determination within 24 hours; 2) notify affected customers via the console and email within 48 hours with recommended mitigations; 3) offer a post-mitigation audit on request.

I flagged one third-party library (libxfer 2.1.3) in the SBOM that had a recent moderate CVE; it's already scheduled for upgrade in next release (see SBOM note).

If everyone signs off I'll produce a final PDF and include a short cover email.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: VM_RFI_response_v1.pdf (29KB stub); PenTest-Summary-Q2-2026.pdf (46KB stub); SBOM-snapshot-2026-09-11.json (11KB stub)

Karthik
